messages:
sam_j: Escalation from ACME (ticket #23456) — private control plane mTLS failures. Customer says their app can't establish the mutual TLS connection to the control plane since ~08:00 UTC. Error on our side: 'tls: handshake error: remote error: bad certificate'. No config changes on their side reported. Can SRE take a look?

eng_oncall: Thanks — can you paste the exact server-side handshake log lines and any client openssl output they sent?

sam_j: Pasting control-plane logs we captured:
```
2026-03-18T08:11:59Z control-plane connection from 10.1.2.3: tls: no certificates presented by client
2026-03-18T08:12:04Z control-plane tls: handshake error: remote error: bad certificate (client=10.1.2.3)
2026-03-18T08:12:04Z control-plane debug: TLS ClientHello SNI='cp.acme.private.redwood'
```

maria_r: Two quick possibilities: 1) client isn't presenting the full cert chain (Verify code 21) or 2) there's TLS interception happening (corp proxy) which terminates TLS and prevents the client cert from reaching our control plane. Ask them for the openssl s_client output and for any corporate proxy/firewall product names.

ben_s: Also ask them to run tcpdump on their egress node and capture the TLS handshake (port 443). If TLS interception is in play you'll often see a local CA (e.g., Zscaler, Blue Coat) in the server cert returned to us or a re-signed cert. Example command to run on their side:
```
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -s 0 -w /tmp/handshake.pcap host cp.acme.private.redwood and port 443
openssl s_client -connect cp.acme.private.redwood:443 -showcerts -servername cp.acme.private.redwood -cert client.pem -key client.key
```

sam_j: Customer returned an openssl snippet (redacted):
```
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 CN = client.acme
verify error:num=21:unable to verify the first certificate
verify return:1
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=client.acme
   i:/CN=ACME-INT
---
---
SSL handshake has read 3500 bytes and written 548 bytes
---
Verify return code: 21 (unable to verify the first certificate)
```

eng_oncall: Verify code 21 indicates the chain isn't trusted — either they didn't include intermediates when presenting the client cert, or the server's configured CA bundle doesn't include the issuing CA. But note earlier server log said 'no certificates presented by client' in at least one connection. That combined with TCP traces we saw from the customer suggests a middlebox may be terminating TLS. Did they mention any outbound inspection (Zscaler/Palo Alto/Bluecoat)?

sam_j: They just replied: 'we route traffic through corporate Zscaler proxy and we have TLS inspection on by default for our egress policy.' They also attached a firewall policy screenshot showing a TLS-inspection rule.

maria_r: That explains it — TLS interception will terminate the client's TLS, and the inspection appliance will not forward the client certificate to our control plane. For mutual TLS you need TCP/TLS passthrough so the full client cert reaches our endpoint. Two remediation paths for them:
- Disable TLS inspection / outbound MITM for cp.acme.private.redwood (recommended).
- Configure a passthrough rule (TCP 443) to our control-plane IPs/FQDN so the proxy does not MITM.

ben_s: Adding concrete networking details to give them: please have them allow outbound TCP 443 (and 10250 if using internal agent tunneling) to these FQDNs/IPs (examples — replace with values from your provisioning email):
```
- cp.acme.private.redwood (SNI-based host; ensure SNI passthrough)
- 34.82.192.10/32
- 34.82.192.11/32
- 52.214.33.72/32
```
Also confirm the proxy allows TLS 1.2+ and doesn't downgrade or strip SNI. If their proxy rewrites SNI, our routing may land on a host expecting a different client cert.

eng_oncall: Ask them to retry with a temporary test: curl using client cert with verbose TLS to see the handshake, e.g.:
```
curl -v --cert client_chain.pem --key client.key https://cp.acme.private.redwood/health
```
They should ensure client_chain.pem contains the client cert followed by any intermediate(s) (client then intermediate). If that works from a machine that bypasses the proxy, but fails from behind the proxy, then it's definitely TLS inspection.

sam_j: Customer tried curl from a machine that bypasses Zscaler — succeeded. From normal corporate laptop (through Zscaler) it fails with TLS handshake error. Customer confirmed they can add an exception. They asked what to whitelist specifically (SNI vs IP).

maria_r: Whitelist SNI/domain for passthrough if their proxy supports that (ideal). If their appliance only supports IP rules, whitelist the control-plane egress IPs. Important: if their device re-signs certificates, mTLS will always break since the client certs never reach us. Also double-check their egress allowlist doesn't NAT the source in a way that drops client cert further upstream.

ben_s: For completeness, also ask them to verify the client presents the full chain: create a file "client_chain.pem" that concatenates client cert then intermediate(s):
```
cat client.crt intermediate.crt > client_chain.pem
```
Then use that as --cert in curl/openssl as above. If client still fails behind the proxy, it's proxy interception.

sam_j: I forwarded steps and suggested temporary whitelist for cp.acme.private.redwood. They confirmed whitelist worked and the app started connecting successfully. Customer will roll the change org-wide and then we'll monitor. Ticket #23456 updated to resolved after customer validation. :white_check_mark: 

netops_bot: Ticket #23456 status -> high -> resolved (updated by sam_j)

eng_oncall: Great — capture remediation steps in the ticket KB: 'mTLS failure due to TLS-inspection/proxy: ensure passthrough for control plane FQDN or whitelist IPs; present full certificate chain from client certs.' I'll add a note to the private onboarding doc to call out TLS-inspection checks.

sam_j: Adding to KB now and will link in the ticket. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
